decisive_items: Negative for MYC, BCL6, and IRF-4 rearrangements
response.rationale: R3 best fits the nodal B-cell biopsy: aberrant BCL2 and elevated Ki-67 with CD5/CD10 negativity and no MYC/BCL6/IRF4 rearrangements favor DLBCL over NLPHL; the chylothorax and bulky adenopathy are complications/distribution of aggressive lymphoma. R2 shares B-cell/BCL2 spans but NLPHL would not explain high Ki-67/aberrant BCL2 or the mediastinal mass. R4 only captures chylothorax, R5 lacks HHV8/effusion-only phenotype, and R6 lacks compatible histology.

rejected.why: PEL requires HHV8/EBV and typically presents as effusion-only without nodal B-cell/BCL2 phenotype; here biopsy shows B lymphocytes with BCL2 and extensive adenopathy.
Chylothorax is supported by the triglyceride level but is a complication of the underlying lymphoma, not the primary diagnosis.
Castleman disease would show characteristic lymph node histology, not aberrant BCL2/elevated Ki-67 in a B-cell population.
